📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been reviewing laptops for well over a decade, sometimes testing more than 30 devices per year. Not all are winners, and many should be avoided, no matter how slick the marketing or how cheap the discount. Good news: It’s my job to recommend laptops that fit your budget and won’t make you regret your purchase six months later. These are my favorite laptops that I’ve tested myself and would highly recommend you buy.

Recent findings suggest that for more guidance, also see my recommendations in specific categories, such as the Best MacBooks, Best Gaming Laptops, Best Chromebooks, Best Budget Laptops, Best Windows Laptops, and Best 2-in-1 Laptops. My guide on How to Choose a Laptop may also help if you’re undecided.

It has been revealed that updated November 2026: I’ve updated my recommendations to include the latest PROLED MacBook Pro that I recently reviewed. I’ve also adjusted my picks throughout and checked prices.

When friends or family ask what laptop to buy, I always start with the MacBook Air. It is far more powerful than its compact size suggests. It’s a shame about the recent $200 price increase from $1,099 to $1,299, but even at that new price, it remains my top pick because it nails the big picture. Everything from the trackpad to the speakers is of the highest quality, and it delivers all the performance and battery life the average person needs.

Recent findings suggest that with the latest M5 chip, its GPU matches the M3 Pro MacBook Pro, easily handling everything from gaming to video editing. That’s not at all what the MacBook Air is designed for, but the performance is there when you want to dabble. It’s what makes it feel like a do-it-all machine, all contained in a fanless chassis that’s still one of the thinnest laptops you can buy. Oh, and did I mention it’ll last well over a full workday away from the wall socket and perform just as well on battery as when plugged in? In almost every aspect, it’s the gold standard.

According to recent reports, while the lower price of the new MacBook Neo might be tempting, the MacBook Air is the better choice for anyone working at a computer all day. With its superior performance, extra memory, faster storage, and Thunderbolt ports, you will never have to question if you have the right tool for the job. (And unless you already know you need a MacBook Pro, you probably don’t.).

Recent findings suggest that speaking of price, I have to mention the new Dell XPS 13 next. I like just about everything about this laptop, whether it’s the compact size, the excellent build quality, or the gorgeous screen. It’s not OLED, but it’s sharp, bright, and color-accurate. It also includes a 120-Hz refresh rate, which makes animation and motion on the device look super smooth. The XPS 13 is filled with features like that, which don’t normally end up in a laptop at this price. While it doesn’t have what I’d call powerhouse performance, the Intel Wildcat Lake chip inside gets the job done for basic, day-to-day computing tasks. That translates to great, all-day battery life, competitive with the MacBook Air. Just don’t try to play games, edit high-resolution video, or take it to engineering school.

According to recent reports, the XPS 13 is especially good for those who want a compact device to travel with. With its tiny bezels, it’s still one of the best laptops to use on a plane. But even beyond that, it’s just one of the best laptops you can buy under $1,000 right now. The Dell XPS 13 is primarily being talked about as a budget laptop, thanks to its $700 starting configuration. But that model comes with only 8 GB of RAM, which limited performance in my testing. You’ll probably just want to avoid that 8 GB model. Most people will want the upgraded 16 GB model, which you can get for $900. It’s the best hardware you can buy for under $1,000.

Industry observers note that if you want a Windows laptop that still feels high-end but has a bit more performance, I would point you to the HP OmniBook Ultra 14. It might be the prettiest Windows laptop you can buy right now. The device is beautifully built and incredibly sturdy, with a thin chassis, an oversized haptic trackpad, and polished metal edges. I also appreciate the three Thunderbolt 4 ports split between both sides for convenient charging, as well as the surprisingly good speakers. I tested the high-end model, which features a fast Snapdragon X2 Elite, 32 GB of RAM, and a gorgeous 2880 x 1800 OLED display. The screen offers near-perfect colors, excellent brightness, and astounding HDR performance. It doesn’t get much better than this. It’s usually quite expensive, but we’re finally seeing discounts that bring it to a more reasonable price. There’s also an Intel model with a very efficient, powerful chip that would be a good choice. I’d go with whichever is cheaper right now.

Sources indicate that and lastly, for something with a larger screen, I’d recommend the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x. It’s a particularly good alternative to the 15-inch MacBook Air, at a much lower cost. These days, you can buy the upgraded model with a 2560 x 1600 OLED display (and a 165-Hz refresh rate) for $1,000 on sale at Amazon. While it’s slightly thicker than the MacBook Air, it leaves more room for extra ports, including HDMI, USB-A, and an SD card slot. And while the Snapdragon X2 Plus isn’t quite an M5 killer, I was happy with the performance and battery life provided. Lenovo also sells a cheaper version directly, but it has a lower-resolution IPS screen that I haven’t tested. The $30 it costs to upgrade the display to a higher-resolution OLED is well worth it.

Sources indicate that while “cheap” means something different to everyone, the best budget laptops generally fall under $750. This is where Windows truly shines, offering great specs for less money. Thanks to the latest processors from Qualcomm and Intel, these laptops now offer battery life that rivals Apple. The best affordable laptop I’ve checked out is the HP OmniBook 5. The model I tested has a Snapdragon X processor, 16 GB of RAM, 512 GB of storage, and a 14-inch OLED screen. Discounts fluctuate frequently, but HP always has some version of the OmniBook 5 with a Snapdragon CPU for around $700 or so. The specific discounted configuration seems to change every few days, though, so shop carefully. I’ll be testing the latest model soon, which switches to Intel processors and starts at $699.

Sources indicate that I also recently tested the newly introduced HP OmniBook 3, which uses the same chip as the OmniBook 5. It frequently sells for less than the OmniBook 5 by at least $100 or so. HP is selling this configuration of the 14-inch model for under $550. While the OmniBook 3 is a good alternative, the OmniBook 5 is much thinner and looks more modern. Neither laptop has a particularly great touchpad, though, which is easily the biggest flaw in both laptops. Between the two, the OmniBook 5 is the better buy if you can afford it.

Sources indicate that the MacBook Neo is Apple’s new entry-level laptop. It launched at an aggressive $599, but that price has recently risen to $699. Even at that price, the laptop shines when it comes to the display. It offers the best screen you can find at this price, bringing the macOS experience to an unprecedented value, even at $699 (or $799 for the 512 GB model). Apple clearly prioritized the front-of-screen experience, delivering a premium feel across the display, build quality, and keyboard. While the 8 GB of RAM, outdated ports, and slower SSD are notable drawbacks—making the MacBook Air a far better choice for remote workers—the Neo is an extremely premium-feeling laptop available for students, travelers, and casual customers. Thanks to the lower-powered A18 Pro chip, though, performance does take a hit. So, be careful about buying this laptop if you work on a computer all day.

Recent findings suggest that given how good some of these budget laptops are, it’s a bit harder to find a place for Chromebooks. Perhaps that’s why Google introduced the next evolution of the platform, so to speak: the Googlebook. The first batch has been released into the world, and I’ve tested a number of them. Googlebooks are similar to Chromebooks in use case, but they run entirely on Android and include some exclusive Google Gemini features. I like the close integration with Android, but Googlebooks ended up being a bit of a letdown, mostly because they’re so expensive. The Acer Googlebook 14 and Dell XPS Googlebook are the two standouts in my book, as both use a Snapdragon X-series chip to deliver really great battery life. The XPS Googlebook is particularly pretty, with a chassis nearly identical to the XPS 13. But $999 is a tough price to swallow. It ultimately has some of the same limitations as Chromebooks: you can’t download applications from the web and must rely on the Google Play Store. The Acer Googlebook 14 is probably my top pick, as it’s the cheapest at $899. Even that isn’t exactly what I’d call a “budget laptop,” though.

It has been revealed that that’s why I strongly recommend the Acer Chromebook Plus Spin 514, especially when it’s on sale for under $700 (which happens often). It uses an efficient (and responsive) MediaTek Kompanio Ultra that delivers excellent battery life. For most people, I wouldn’t recommend spending over $500 on a Chromebook; if you’re paying more, consider the MacBook Neo or the HP OmniBooks, which offer more than a Chromebook’s limited scope. But the Acer Chromebook Plus Spin 514 might be the best combination of display, touchpad, and battery life at this price, making it a good choice for the right person—so long as you know what you’re paying for.

Industry observers note that truly cheap Chromebooks come with bigger compromises, especially in display quality, touchpad feel, and battery life. If you really need something dirt cheap as a starter laptop for a kid or as a secondary device, I’d recommend the Asus Chromebook CX14. It has a modern design, enough ports, a good keyboard, and decent storage.

The laptops above are great for most people, but content creators and gamers need extra performance. No option is better than the new OLED (or PROLED, as Apple calls it) MacBook Pro. No laptop feels more premium than the MacBook Pro, combining incredible performance with the brightest OLED screen ever put in a laptop. The brightness levels have never been seen on an OLED laptop before, making this the dream machine for producing and consuming HDR content. Regardless of what you’re doing, you’ll certainly notice the difference. It’s also the first MacBook Pro to get a touchscreen, a long-awaited feature.

Industry observers note that I should mention, though, that it doesn’t take a step forward in terms of performance. For the first time since this generation of MacBook Pro launched in 2021, it uses the same M5 Pro or M5 Max internally. With rumors that the M6 Pro and M6 Max are being skipped entirely, you’ll have to accept that you’re paying a lot more for the same performance. To make the decision harder, Apple still sells the previous-gen model—so you’ll have to decide whether the upgraded screen is worth the $400 extra. For my money, it totally is.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Windows has made its first successful attempt to properly compete with the MacBook Pro. I’m talking primarily about the launch of Nvidia’s newly introduced RTX Spark “superchip” and the new laptops that use it. To be clear, despite Nvidia’s involvement, these aren’t gaming laptops. Like the MacBook Pro, they’re designed first and foremost for running heavier creative applications and on-device AI. The Surface Laptop Ultra is a great example, which has a lot in common with the standard 15-inch Surface Laptop. But the differences internally are substantial. The Surface Laptop Ultra uses a single chip that integrates the CPU, GPU, and memory together, allowing up to 128 GB of memory to be shared across the system. That’s not unlike how Apple Silicon works, dramatically increasing on-device AI performance. So, if you’ve been curious about running LLMs right on your laptop without relying on the cloud, these RTX Spark laptops are a great place to start. The other two RTX Spark laptops I tested, the HP OmniBook Ultra 16 and Lenovo Pro 9n, share a lot with the Surface Laptop Ultra (including performance). The OmniBook Ultra is the thinnest of the three, but I prefer the Surface Laptop Ultra’s Mini-LED display and 3:2 aspect ratio.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most common use for extra laptop performance, however, is gaming. If you proposal to boot up graphically intensive games more than a couple of times a week, you will want a dedicated gaming laptop. After testing dozens over the past year, I’ve come back to the Lenovo LOQ 15 as my top pick. There are cheaper RTX 5050 models, such as the Alienware 15 or MSI Cyborg A15, but prices have been increasing on these laptops over the past few months. The Alienware 15 with the RTX 5050, in particular, has seen a $600 price jump, which makes it incredibly overpriced.

That’s led me back to the LOQ 15, which has stayed steady at $1,300 at Walmart and gives you an RTX 5060 for graphics and a bright, colorful screen. You won’t find a cheaper gaming laptop that doesn’t make some significant compromises in either performance or screen quality, both of which can sour the gaming experience. And while I wish the LOQ 15 were still selling for under $1,000 as it did at launch, it’s still the best gaming laptop for the money right now. It’s really the only gaming laptop under $1,500 I’d currently buy, given where prices are.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also a whole world of gaming laptops outside the budget tier, though. I’ve tested an assortment of options, and I always come back to the Razer Blade 14 and Razer Blade 16. Portable, minimalist, and extremely well-made, their sleek design works just as well for school or work as it does for gaming, without the bulk of a traditional gaming laptop. While you can buy more powerful options, nothing quite matches the Razer Blade. They’re expensive, but if you can afford them, they’re as premium as gaming laptops get. I’ll soon be testing the latest version of the Blade 16, which includes Intel’s fresh Panther Lake chips and should offer vastly improved battery life.

If you choose one of the laptops above, you will be very happy with your purchase. However, if you are looking for a specific feature or a different price point, I have included a few other options below that I’ve recently reviewed and enjoyed using. Each of these recently tested laptops has at least one minor drawback, but they could still be the perfect choice depending on your needs and current discounts.

Sources indicate that framework Laptop 13 Pro for $1,599: We’ve always loved Framework laptops at WIRED, mainly because their internal components are so repairable and upgradable. Users can easily swap out nearly every part, including the CPU. The Framework Laptop 13 Pro uses the same internal structure as the basic Framework Laptop 13, but upgraded with a haptic touchpad, an aluminum chassis, and a brighter (and sharper) display. The result is the Framework Laptop I’ve always wanted, especially with an all-black aesthetic that hints at ThinkPad inspiration. But most of all, if you’re going to try and make a laptop last for many years, it makes sense that it would be something more premium. This one actually feels like it’s worth the investment.

In a recent development, microsoft Surface Laptop 13.8 for $1,000: The Surface Laptop 13.8 (also known as the 7th Edition) was one of my favorite laptops throughout 2024 and 2025, primarily because of its premium build quality, great battery life, and 3:2 aspect ratio screen. And while I still love this laptop, it’s risen dramatically in price and no longer feels like a great value, especially since it’s two years old now. The 2024 model now starts at $1,200, though I’ve occasionally seen it dip under $1,000. The next-generation model with the Snapdragon X2 chips costs $1,700, but I have seen that price come down as low as $1,250 on discount.

Dell 14 Plus for $1,172: There was a time—2025, to be exact—when the Dell 14 Plus was as affordable as $600. It was easily the best deal in the world of Windows laptops, primarily because the Dell 14 Plus has a 2560 x 1600 display and a smooth touchpad—two things laptops at that price typically lack. These days, it’s up to over $1,000, though for a 1 TB configuration, that is still a reasonable price. The XPS 13 is the better overall laptop, but the Dell 14 Plus offers more ports and storage for the price.

Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 Ultra for $2,250: I like this laptop quite a bit. The OLED screen is sharp, bright, and quite colorful—very similar to the HP OmniBook Ultra. It also has many of the other great features on premium Windows laptops these days, including a haptic-feedback touchpad and a very slim profile. Unfortunately, it’s only available right now in a very expensive, maxed-out configuration with 32 GB of RAM and at least a terabyte of storage. I don’t think that’s a good pairing for this ultra-light laptop. Even with half the memory and storage, though, this would be too expensive compared to the competition.

Recent findings suggest that macBook Pro M5 for $1,999: It’s not a significant step up from the MacBook Air in performance, and it’s much thicker. You’re paying for the Mini-LED screen and extra ports. Unfortunately, compared to the other MacBook models, it got a $300 price bump to $1,999. On discount, you’ll often find it selling for $1,799, though, which is solid for the specs.

Sources indicate that asus Zenbook A16 for $2,200: The Zenbook A14 and A16 are Asus’ ultralight laptops, weighing just 2.16 pounds, making them some of the lightest laptops you can buy right now. This second-generation Zenbook A16 is still incredibly light and now comes with second-generation Snapdragon X2 chips. It’s unique for its portability, and the Qualcomm chips deliver great battery life and performance. However, given the dramatic price increase, I’d suggest buying the 2025 model instead, which consistently comes in under $1,000.

Recent findings suggest that alienware 16X Aurora for $2,575: Another solid gaming laptop with the typical Alienware flair. Its standout features are its higher-resolution display and great build quality. The price fluctuates frequently, though, and in most cases, the LOQ 15 is the better option (unless you really want that sharper OLED screen, which is this laptop’s best quality).

Industry observers note that asus Googlebook 14: While I love the Android integration and the beauty of this hardware, this particular Googlebook is far too expensive for what these devices can actually do. They fill a very familiar role to Chromebooks, and yet, these first Googlebooks all have 16 GB of RAM for some reason. This one just doesn’t earn its $1,200 price tag.

Industry observers note that dell 14S: This is the 2026 successor to the Dell 14 Plus, which I recommended above. This is a solid laptop with a premium design and a highly reflective OLED display. It also performs well, thanks to the latest Intel Core Ultra Series 3 chip. But it’s far too expensive right now. Until the price comes down, I prefer just about every other Dell option, including the Dell 14 Plus, Dell XPS 13, or Dell XPS 14.

Lenovo LOQ 15 Essential: This is a “upcoming” model that came out this year, even though it uses a CPU from 2023. But honestly, this is just too expensive. I’ve seen it on sale for under $1,400, but even then, the standard LOQ 15 costs about the same and has a far superior display.

Acer Swift 16 AI: This is one of the few laptops you can buy with the powerful, efficient new Intel Core Ultra X9 chips. However, the Acer Swift 16 AI takes an experimental approach with its oversized trackpad, making it very difficult to use. Even at a discount, you’ll find it frustrating.

In a recent development, asus TUF Gaming A14: There’s a lot I like about this gaming laptop. The design is portable yet modern, and the display is sharp. And while the TUF Gaming A14 is impressive technically (using the interesting AMD Strix Point chip), the lack of a discrete graphics card doesn’t provide enough gaming performance to justify its very high price. I haven’t tested the options with dedicated graphics cards, but they tend to be more expensive than counterparts from Lenovo, Acer, or Alienware.

According to recent reports, asus Vivobook 14: I recommended this laptop a lot throughout 2025, but it doesn’t hold up as well these days. While the Vivobook 14 has great battery life, the HP OmniBook 5 14 offers a much better display and similar specs, making it a better laptop.

How Much Should You Spend on a Laptop?

According to recent reports, if you’re shopping for a laptop, you probably already have a budget. But some context might help put things in perspective. The cheapest laptops cost around $200, but laptop prices can range as high as $5,000. Meanwhile, the average amount people spend, according to the best data we have, is around $750. That lands decidedly in the midrange, splitting between the more expensive devices that are more than $1,000 and the budget-tier machines you find below $700.

When we talk about pricing, it’s often the “starting” price of the laptop, meaning the lowest-priced configuration. This is really notable to consider, as you want to compare devices apples to apples as much as possible. For example, a cheaper laptop might start at $750 with 256 GB of storage, while a more premium laptop might start at this same price but come with 512 GB or even 1 TB of storage. Increasingly, you can find some really decent laptops around this price, some of which we’ve listed.

Recent findings suggest that if your budget needs to be under $750, though, there are still good options. Laptops below this price tend to come with compromises. Most commonly, it’s the quality of the display and touchpad that suffers, as these are things you can’t gauge from a spec sheet or reference photo. Or it might be a performance-related glitch, such as the 8 GB of memory in the MacBook Neo. If you’re shopping for something under $500, Chromebooks often give you the best bang for your buck.

So, why spend more? Well, there are two primary reasons. First, you might want a more premium design, perhaps one that has a more daring aesthetic or high-end components. Take the MacBook Pro, for example. It starts at $600 more than the MacBook Air but comes with a brighter mini-LED screen, significantly better speakers, and more ports. The second primary reason to spend more than $750 or so is to get more performance. Whether for gaming or content creation, laptops with discrete GPUs cost more, which is why it’s hard to find a worthwhile gaming laptop for less than $1,000. If you’re buying a gaming laptop, plan to spend a few hundred bucks more.

What Are the Best Laptop Brands?

It has been revealed that unlike the smartphone world, the biggest laptop brands have been around for more than 40 years. Besides Apple, four laptop brands stand out for adopting the latest technology and trends while providing reliable support and service.

According to recent reports, lenovo is the biggest PC brand in the world, at least in terms of global shipments. It’s perhaps most well-known for its familiar sub-brands like ThinkPad and Yoga, but it also isn’t afraid to take risks with more experimental designs and advanced technology. Lenovo has also made a name for itself in the gaming space with its Legion laptops, known for balancing performance and features at competitive prices.

Asus has quickly become a favorite, notable for the sheer number of laptops available in the consumer market. The company takes a similar approach to Lenovo, which has led Asus to innovate quickly on fresh technology and designs while also launching premium laptops at more affordable prices than its competitors. Gaming, in particular, is a space Asus has come to dominate, with the ROG Zephyrus, Strix, and TUF brands leading the way.

Dell and HP are generally more conservative, but both have recently undergone significant rebranding. In 2024, HP replaced its Spectre and Envy lines with the OmniBook name. Meanwhile, Dell briefly retired its well-known Inspiron and XPS sub-brands in 2025, though it has since reversed course and brought the XPS line back.

Other notable laptop brands include Microsoft Surface, Samsung, Acer, LG, and MSI, though none have the same global footprint as the top four.

How Do I Choose the Right Laptop?

In a recent development, if none of these laptops resonate with what you’re looking for, that’s OK! There are far more laptops than we have time to test. To help you make smart choices, we put together a complete laptop buying guide. We also cover the CPUs and GPUs you need to know. We recommend sticking to these guidelines:.

In a recent development, RAM: We recommend 16 GB of RAM. That’s become the fresh standard, even in more affordable laptops. Upgrading to 32 GB is even better, so you won’t have to worry about running out of memory, especially if you’re a gamer or video editor. The recent memory shortage has led to some dramatic price increases, largely based on configurations of RAM. Apple’s launch of the 8 GB MacBook Neo this spring has led to the return of high-end 8-GB Windows laptops as well, such as the Dell XPS 13.

Sources indicate that CPU: For Windows laptops, you have three CPU brands to choose from: Intel, AMD, or Qualcomm. Intel’s Core Ultra Series 2 introduced in late 2024 and delivers a huge boost to battery life. It also has the best integrated graphics of the three. Core Ultra Series 3 is just now rolling out and, based on my testing, is extremely impressive in performance and efficiency. While AMD chips are primarily used in gaming laptops, they’ve struggled to gain ground on Intel elsewhere.

Industry observers note that qualcomm’s Snapdragon X chips, however, have seriously challenged Intel over the past year with their ARM architecture, offering some of the best battery life we’ve ever seen on Windows machines. The second generation, Snapdragon X2, was confirmed last fall and rolled out slowly throughout 2026. They improve performance, but in many cases, they've led to more expensive laptops, while previous-gen laptops are still available that cost less.

Starting this year, there’s also the choice of Nvidia’s latest RTX Spark platform, which gives you the option of 18-core or 20-core CPUs. More on that in the GPU section below.

Apple Silicon is what powers all the modern MacBooks, the latest of which is the M5 chip. Read our in-depth guide on Which MacBook to Buy for more information.

It has been revealed that graphics: Want to play AAA PC games, edit video on your laptop, or run local AI models? You’ll want some powerful graphics on hand. At this point, Nvidia is the primary option. The RTX 5090, launched in 2025, is still the most powerful newly introduced GPU available, but the 5040-series remains a good option.

Industry observers note that integrated graphics have improved significantly over the years, though, especially on processors made by Apple, AMD, and Intel, such as the Apple M5 or the Intel Core Ultra X9 388H. Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform uses a single “superchip” that provides unified memory to both the CPU and GPU to improve AI performance.

Screen: The display depends highly on the size of the laptop. A 1,200-pixel resolution (HD+) screen on a 13- or 14-inch laptop looks sharp enough to get by, but you’ll want more pixels on larger displays, such as a 2560 x 1600, 2880 x 1800, or 3840 x 2400. While IPS screens are good enough for most people, OLED and Mini-LED are becoming more common, offering better color accuracy, deeper contrast, and excellent HDR performance.

Connectivity: We generally recommend at least two USB-C ports, along with one HDMI and one USB-A port for legacy devices. (Remember that nearly all laptops today use one of those USB-C ports for the power adapter.) Thankfully, most laptops still have headphone jacks, but always check, because a few models have dropped them. Lastly, make sure it supports Wi-Fi 6E or newer. Even if you don’t have a Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 router yet, you’ll likely have one in the future (see our Best Routers or Best Mesh Systems guides if you need a new one).

Industry observers note that battery life: Battery life is extremely competitive these days, with Apple, Qualcomm, and Intel all making highly ambitious battery-life claims. Most laptops with the latest chips (and without discrete graphics) will get you more than 10 hours of battery life, or many more if your workload is lighter.

As mentioned, in Windows-based laptops, there are three primary options for CPUs: Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. All three companies offer good processors, but it really depends on the type of laptop. For premium laptops, you’ll want something like the Intel Core Ultra 258V or Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite. Meanwhile, for budget laptops, Snapdragon X is the best choice. And for gaming laptops, I’d recommend something from AMD, such as the Ryzen AI 9 365. All three companies have announced next-gen chips for 2026, and there’s some exciting stuff coming soon.

Intel’s latest chips, known as either Core Ultra Series 3 or codename Panther Lake, are slowly rolling out in new laptops, such as the Dell XPS 14. These chips represent a massive leap forward in both CPU and integrated graphics performance. While highly impressive, they will soon face fresh competition from upcoming AMD and Qualcomm releases.

Industry observers note that qualcomm made a major impact in 2024 with its Snapdragon X chips. Similar to Apple’s M-series, these ARM-based processors prioritize efficiency to drastically improve battery life. This has been a game-changer for Windows laptops across different price points. The Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite is the highest-end option for performance, but the Snapdragon X Plus and base Snapdragon X still offer equally strong battery life, despite showing up in much cheaper laptops. The sequel was unveiled in late 2025, and now in 2026, we’re seeing those laptops roll out. Unfortunately, like Intel’s latest chips, laptops with this next-gen silicon tend to be significantly more expensive than their predecessors.

It has been revealed that AMD has grown into a competitive player in the gaming laptop space. Its latest processors, including the Ryzen 9 9950X3D and 9900X3D, are the most powerful gaming chips you can find in a laptop. Unfortunately, it’s still hard to find many laptops supporting these killer chips. AMD also offers its Ryzen AI 300 H and HX chips, which are more commonly found in gaming laptops. While they also offer a mainstream Ryzen AI 300 series, these chips aren’t found in many laptops and currently fall short of the battery life offered by Intel and Qualcomm.

In a recent development, nvidia’s RTX Spark platform just hit the scene, promising to deliver power and efficiency, especially when running AI-based operations. It’s not as ubiquitous as Intel, AMD, or Qualcomm chips, but it’s something to watch for.

I have been reviewing laptops for well over a decade, and WIRED contributor Chris Null has been testing them for 25 years. We test each laptop we review in a variety of situations, including both synthetic benchmark tests and real-world use cases. We make comparisons against similar equipment. We don’t just look at the specs—our reviews evaluate performance, usability, portability, and price to help you find the right laptop for your needs.

We put every laptop through a gauntlet of tests before writing a review and assigning a rating.

Hands-on use: We evaluate the exterior of the device. We compare how thin and light it is against other laptops. We repeatedly open and close the lid to test the quality and ease of the hinge. We push on weak points like the keyboard and lid to test build quality. We also extensively test the keyboard and touchpad for comfort and precision. By using each laptop as our daily driver for days or even weeks, we can spot real-world quirks—like awkward port placement, excessive bloatware, or unexpected problems that may make the laptop difficult to use—that you won’t see on a spec sheet.

Sights and sounds: Once we boot up the device, it’s all about the sights and sounds. The screen is paramount, as it’s your window into everything the laptop has to offer. While you can tell a lot about brightness, color, and contrast just by looking, we go beyond subjective testing. We use a Spyder colorimeter to precisely measure brightness, contrast, color saturation, and accuracy. For HDR-capable screens, we also test peak brightness with HDR content. Finally, we evaluate the webcam and speakers to ensure they are ready for your video calls and streaming sessions.

Performance testing: Finally, we test performance. We always evaluate a laptop based on what it’s intended for—we don’t expect a $500 budget laptop to run like a gaming powerhouse, or a gaming rig to get 18 hours of battery life. Our testbed includes more than 20 synthetic benchmarks, which we constantly adapt based on the device's CPU and operating system. These include tests within Geekbench, PCMark, 3DMark, Procyon, GFXBench, Puget Bench, Superposition, Cinebench, and various gaming-related tests such as 3DMark and Cyberpunk 2077. While we don’t generally report raw scores, we pay close attention to what they tell us. We also monitor fan noise, surface temperature, and overall battery life during these tests.

It has been revealed that it’s a lot, I know. But we’re thorough, because we want to stand by our recommendations and ensure that the laptops we rate highly are worth the money.

Recent findings suggest that why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

I was captivated by the idea of a 3D printer designed for children, so I jumped at the chance to let my nine-year-old try the Funbox. She’s wanted a 3D printer for ages. I’ve held out, partly because of the cost and partly because of the inevitable tide of tiny plastic things that would end up around the house.

In a recent development, the Funbox is a compact, good-looking printer made by Ugee. It's fully enclosed for safety, has a clean air filter, is anti-scald and you can create with just a tap via the app. With Christmas coming up, plenty of parents will be hunting for the right option for their kids, so I want to be honest about whether this is it. Does this compare to the best 3D printers?

Sources indicate that the external design is delightful. Ugee has nailed the look for kids: it’s cute, it has minimal buttons and fuss, and mine arrived in baby blue. A pack of stickers in the box lets your child decorate it themselves.

Industry observers note that the inside is just as accessible. The build plate is easy to put in place and everything is clearly marked to show you how to get started (although we did make a wrong turn by not actually putting the plate in the first time around as you can see above – oops!).

According to recent reports, loading filament is simple, though it can be a bit fiddly for small fingers. It is pretty much plug and play – setup took me about 20 minutes, and my daughter was able to manage the first print pretty much independently with minimal interference, only some instruction. Bear in mind, the build space is small, so this printer is best for smaller prints. You can keep an eye on your print via the camera, which links to the app – my daughter was fascinated by this part.

Designs come from a marketplace in the Funbox app, available for mobile or tablet. It should be simple to use, but it’s glitchy. On our Huion tablet, the ‘start’ button was hidden behind the notch and there was no way to scroll or move the screen to reach it. That forced us onto the mobile app, which wasn’t ideal when I wanted my daughter to use the printer independently, without borrowing my phone.

For the most part, the Funbox worked as expected. My daughter could pick a print and start it herself, and she really enjoyed the process.

Recent findings suggest that the small build volume is the main constraint. Many designs have to be printed in parts and assembled, which is fine if you stick to small prints. For anything more complex, you’ll need to be ready to help with sticking or putting pieces together. It also prints in a single colour at a time.

Most of the toys we printed turned out well, especially single-piece prints with no moving parts. The detail was good, and the results matched what the marketplace listings promised. Highlights include a cat hair comb, a skull and crossbones hair slide and a phone holder, which would hold my phone if it was the right size (note: must check next time).

Recent findings suggest that functional toys were a different story. We made a couple of fidget toys that couldn’t do their job without breaking. That could be down to the third-party design, or to the filament being too brittle for the purpose. We couldn’t tell which.

That fits what this printer is: a starter machine built for fun, not one that delivers polished, fully functional prints every time.

According to recent reports, we haven’t yet tested the AI 3D model builder, which turns your child’s drawing into a printable 3D model. We’ll cover our experience of it in a separate piece.

The Funbox costs $299/£318 but is often on sale for $279/£289. Whether that’s reasonable depends on who you're buying it for.

For my nine-year-old, I’d rather take on the steeper learning curve of a basic ‘grown-up’ printer like the Bambu Lab A1, which I’d expect to give better-quality prints for similar money. It’s less approachable for a child to use alone, but the results would be worth it for her. For a younger child, though, the Funbox’s ease of use and friendly design make a stronger case, and I think they justify the price.

Industry observers note that if you want a genuinely child-focused printer, this is a good option. Just be aware you’re trading away print size and complexity.

Choose your designs carefully. Ugee’s own are reliable, but third-party designs from the marketplace are hit and miss.

Recent findings suggest that if your child is at the upper end of the age range (nine to 12), consider a basic printer from one of the adult-focused brands instead. For younger children, the Funbox is the easier fit.

#500. Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1246 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily

Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function.
  • It has been revealed that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time.
  • The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.

It has been revealed that the findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.

According to recent reports, these questions are especially important because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.

In a recent development, to investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.

More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills.

One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.

Recent findings suggest that cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn new things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.

The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.

Industry observers note that "The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.

"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.

Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently.

The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.

Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.

Recent findings suggest that working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing latest information.

Light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.

The differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.

Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity.

The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.

Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.

One possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.

This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.

"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.

"However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is important to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing.".

What the Eight-Year Study Revealed.

The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.

The current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.

Researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.

To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.

Importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the results offer an important perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.

The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.

Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.

The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research.

Watkins shared online.

This experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth.

Industry observers note that when you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments.

According to recent reports, on the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For many astronauts, the spectacular sight of lightning stands out when looking back at Earth from the International Space Station.
  • For astronauts on the International Space Station, looking back to Earth at night can be as dazzling as looking outward toward the stars.
  • In an essay for Air & Space magazine, Donald Pettit, a NASA astronaut and dedicated photographer, described the "spectacular" view of Earth at night visible from the station.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For many astronauts, the spectacular sight of lightning stands out when looking back at Earth from the International Space Station.

For astronauts on the International Space Station, looking back to Earth at night can be as dazzling as looking outward toward the stars.

In an essay for Air & Space magazine, Donald Pettit, a NASA astronaut and dedicated photographer, described the "spectacular" view of Earth at night visible from the station. Cities and civilization, he wrote, looked "like tendrils outlined with the glimmer of a Broadway marquee." Intense, colorful lights cast by clusters of fishing boats across darkened oceans reminded him of "a constellation of stars" forming "unfamiliar members of the Zodiac.".

Sources indicate that NASA astronaut Sally Ride—the first American woman to fly in space—also marveled at the "indescribable" sights of Earth from orbit. Lightning was among the most spectacular, she noted in an essay for the same magazine. "On Earth, people see lightning from below the clouds. In orbit, we see it from above," she wrote. "Bolts of lightning are diffused by the clouds into bursting balls of light. Sometimes, when a storm extends hundreds of miles, it looks like a transcontinental brigade is tossing fireworks from cloud to cloud.".

Sources indicate that all three phenomena—city lights, fishing fleets, and lightning—were on display when the space station passed over the South China Sea near Borneo at 14:20 UTC (9:20 p.m. Western Indonesian Time) on October 28, 2026. When an astronaut captured this scene with a Nikon Z9 camera, several overshooting tops bubbled up from thunderstorms, including two illuminated by lightning flashes. These tall, domelike protrusions rise above a thunderstorm's anvil and sometimes into the stratosphere, indicating strong updrafts and intense storms.

The lights of Singapore, a city-state of 6.2 million people, appear on the left side of the image, with the curving Singapore Strait separating the city from Batam and Bintan islands to the south. The cluster of blue lights west of Singapore, reminiscent of the Pleiades, or Seven Sisters, was likely produced by fishing boats using bright lights to attract squid or schooling fish such as sardines or anchovies. Offshore to the northwest, the scattered orange points are likely gas flares.

For many astronauts, it's the sight of lightning that lingers. "Like fireflies in the night, lightning is my favorite sight from space," noted NASA astronaut Anil Menon in a video of Earth's darkened limb that he posted on X, where pinpoints of lightning flicker almost constantly. Lightning is hard to capture and share, he added, but the video offers the best representation he's seen. "It’s unchanged, at real speed, and shows the vast reach of storms and lightning across earth, plus the rapid flashes that dance across the horizon.".

NASA scientists estimate that there are 2,000 thunderstorms occurring on Earth at any one moment, producing nearly 60 flashes per second—roughly 5 million flashes per day.

The image has been cropped and enhanced to improve contrast, and lens artifacts have been removed. The International Space Station Program supports the laboratory as part of the ISS National Lab to help astronauts take pictures of Earth that will be of the greatest value to scientists and the public, and to make those images freely available on the Internet. The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy.
  • It has been revealed that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words.
  • The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the way people describe their lives may offer surprising clues about their personalities, including traits associated with psychopathy. A upcoming study from the University of Mississippi challenges the familiar image of psychopaths as cold and emotionless, revealing that their patterns of language can be far more complex than expected.

It has been revealed that researchers examined hundreds of personal life stories and discovered that three major traits associated with psychopathy, boldness, meanness, and disinhibition, were connected to distinctly different ways of using words. Some of the findings were particularly unexpected. For example, people who scored higher in meanness tended to use more positive language, while those with greater boldness used fewer words associated with anxiety.

The findings, published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences, suggest that psychopathic traits can influence everyday communication in subtle ways that conventional stereotypes often overlook.

In a recent development, "The goal here is not to diagnose psychopathy based on language," mentioned Ky Bray, an Ole Miss doctoral candidate in psychology. "It's to point to the fact that psychopathy shows up in everyday behaviors, even subtle behaviors like language.

"If we want to understand psychopathy and the different traits that comprise it, we need to think creatively about how these traits shape social interaction.".

What 450 Life Stories Revealed About Psychopathy.

The researchers used a psychological framework known as the Triarchic Model of Psychopathy, which examines three distinct personality dimensions. Boldness generally involves confidence and fearlessness, meanness reflects tendencies toward callousness and reduced empathy, and disinhibition involves difficulties with impulse control. According to Laura Drislane, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of Mississippi, these characteristics can affect ordinary behaviors, including how people describe their own experiences.

In a recent development, to investigate these connections, Drislane and Bray recruited 450 participants, including college students and individuals who reported having been incarcerated. Each person responded to open questions about key moments in their life, including their greatest highs, lowest points, and major turning points.

After writing their personal accounts, participants completed a questionnaire designed to measure their levels of psychopathic traits. The researchers then analyzed the written responses using specialized software that identifies patterns in word choice.

It has been revealed that the analysis focused on how frequently participants used language associated with different psychological categories, including positive and negative emotions, achievement, social influence or clout, and risk. By comparing these language patterns with the personality scores, the team identified several intriguing relationships.

Surprising Differences in Positive and Negative Language.

Participants with higher disinhibition scores generally used more negative words in their personal stories. They were also less likely to mention friends or use language connected to positive emotions and personal achievement.

Sources indicate that meanness, however, showed a very different pattern. People scoring higher in this trait tended to use more positive language, along with more words related to achievement and rewards. They also used fewer expressions associated with negative emotions.

It has been revealed that boldness was associated with another distinctive pattern. Participants with higher scores used fewer anxiety-related words, including terms such as fear, afraid, and worry. Their personal accounts also contained fewer references to mental illness.

These differences suggest that psychopathic traits do not produce a single recognizable style of communication. Instead, different characteristics are associated with different ways of describing emotions, goals, relationships, and personal experiences.

According to recent reports, "What this tells us is the story we tell about our life has meaning," Drislane stated. "It helps people make sense of their experiences, develop a worldview and a coherent sense of who they are.

"What we're starting to see is that in psychopathy, there are traits that relate to differences in meaning-making and the ways people think about their life.".

Why Psychopathy Is More Complex Than the Stereotypes.

The researchers also discovered that the relationship between personality traits and language changed depending on which question participants were answering. Someone describing a difficult experience, for example, might use language differently than when recalling a personal success.

This variation is key because it challenges the assumption that psychopathy is characterized by consistently flat or emotionally empty communication. Instead, the findings indicate that language patterns depend on both the particular psychopathic trait and the context in which someone is telling their story.

"People tend to think of psychopathy as one thing, but it's actually multidimensional," Bray noted. "What we mean when we say that everyone exists on this spectrum. Everyone has some degree of meanness, boldness, and disinhibition.

"Viewing it from a multidimensional perspective allows us to observe how those traits might manifest in nonforensic populations, in people who have not committed a crime. That allows us to see how these traits affect college students, business professionals, or interpersonal relationships.".

Industry observers note that like many personality conditions, psychopathy is better understood as a spectrum rather than a simple distinction between people who have it and those who do not. At one extreme is the familiar cultural image of a "psychopath," while people at the opposite end score low in all three dimensions.

It has been revealed that this approach allows researchers to examine psychopathic traits throughout the general population, including among people who have never committed a crime. It also helps explain why the same broad label can encompass individuals with very different personalities and behaviors.

How Understanding Psychopathic Traits Could Improve Treatment.

Recent findings suggest that recognizing these differences has implications beyond understanding everyday speech. Researchers have linked dimensions of psychopathy to serious outcomes, including criminal behavior, repeat offending, and intimate partner violence. Examining each trait separately may provide a clearer picture of how these risks develop.

Recent findings suggest that "That's in part why there's a movement away from calling people 'psychopaths,' because we don't view psychopathy as a category," Drislane said. "But psychopathic dimensions can predict notable outcomes, things like crime, recidivism, or intimate partner violence.

"What our research, including this paper, suggests is that it's important to look beyond that label and into the different components or dimensions of psychopathy, because each of those dimensions actually has a unique set of outcomes or things that it can predict.".

Recent findings suggest that researchers also emphasize that psychopathy can be treated, with interventions aimed at reducing problematic symptoms and behaviors. Understanding the psychological processes behind boldness, meanness, and disinhibition could help scientists develop more targeted approaches and potentially identify ways to prevent severe problems from emerging.

According to recent reports, "If we want to be able to treat or ideally even prevent psychopathy from developing, we need to understand the mechanisms at play," she noted. "That comes down to understanding the unique contributors for all three of these dimensions.".

Trmnl’s latest digital dashboard features a large color E Ink screen to display photos and artwork.﻿.

Trmnl’s latest digital dashboard features a large color E Ink screen to display photos and artwork.﻿.

It has been revealed that trmnl, a manufacturer best known for its highly customizable E Ink dashboards that can function as anything from a desktop calendar to a stock tracker, has introduced a newly introduced display that’s also well suited for showing artwork and photos. It’s not the company’s first color E Ink device, but instead of being limited to just four colors, the new Frame can display thousands of shades using a 31.5-inch E Ink Spectra 6 panel, similar to what you’ll find in products from Aura and Pocketbook.

The Frame is now available for preorder for $1,299 in a handmade wooden body and you can choose from four different types of wood: white oak, cherry, sapele, and walnut. The first batch will be a limited run of around 470 units that’s already more than half sold out, and delivery of most of the displays is expected to happen in early 2027. Optional add-ons include a matching wooden kickstand if you don’t want to hang it on a wall, and a larger 20,000mAh battery. However, the Frame should run for months between charges with the standard 10,000mAh option.

What sets the Frame apart from other large format E Ink art frames and posters is that it’s open source and can do more than display images. Through plugins you can build yourself, or download from a marketplace featuring over 1,400 at this point, the Frame can also be used as a dashboard showing the weather, to-do lists, or whatever info you want hanging on your wall.

If you do use it for displaying imagery, Trmnl developed Lazarus, a color conversion engine the manufacturer believes provides the “best color matching on the market for any Spectra 6 display.” If you disagree, because the Frame is open source, you can adjust the color tuning to match your own preferences.

As with Trmnl’s other E Ink products, the Frame can be connected to the internet to dynamically display whatever information you need it to. But to further extend its battery life, you can also fill a microSD card with a folder of images files and use the Frame offline. You can customize how frequently a new photo is displayed, or set up schedules so that your favorite piece of art stays on screen longer than others. While the Frame is more expensive than other E Ink Spectra 6 products currently available, the appeal here is the flexibility to use it as more than just a digital poster.

#491. Tech Report: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1606 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily

Tech Report: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover.
  • The mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
  • When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover. But before researchers can determine whether this subtle signal reveals something extraordinary about the cosmos, they must answer a crucial question: Is the effect actually coming from the universe, or could it be an illusion created by the telescopes observing it?

The mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang. This ancient light provides a remarkable snapshot of the "baby universe" as it existed nearly 13.8 billion years ago, allowing scientists to investigate conditions from the earliest stages of cosmic history.

When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space. As radiation scattered off free electrons during this transition, it acquired a small amount of linear polarization. Polarization describes the direction in which light's electric field oscillates, and a similar effect occurs when sunlight scatters through Earth's atmosphere.

It has been revealed that now, observations suggest that the polarization of this ancient radiation may have shifted slightly as the light traveled across the universe. This possible rotation, called cosmic birefringence, is especially intriguing because it could point to physical processes not explained by the Standard Model, the leading theory describing fundamental particles and their interactions. Confirming the effect might even provide new insights into dark matter and dark energy (see Sidebar).

A Mysterious Cosmic Signal or a Telescope Error?

According to recent reports, there is a major obstacle to interpreting this potential discovery. An extremely small error in how a telescope's polarization detectors are aligned can produce a signal that looks almost identical to cosmic birefringence.

Sources indicate that to help address this problem, physicists at the University of California San Diego developed a newly introduced technique for checking how accurately different groups of detectors measure polarization angles. They tested their approach using existing observations collected by the European Space Agency's Planck satellite, which mapped the universe's ancient radiation in extraordinary detail.

The research was led by Postdoctoral Fellow Anto I. Lonappan, Chancellor's Distinguished Professor of Physics Brian Keating, and Associate Professor of Physics Kam Arnold. Their findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Separating Real Cosmic Effects From Instrument Errors.

Previous studies have suggested that the polarization of the CMB may have rotated by just a fraction of a degree over its nearly 14 billion years of travel. Although that sounds insignificant, such a tiny change could have enormous implications for fundamental physics.

Unfortunately, a telescope whose polarization detectors are misaligned by a similarly small angle could produce precisely the same apparent rotation. If every detector shares the same alignment error, the resulting measurements cannot distinguish that error from a genuine rotation of the cosmic signal.

The UC San Diego researchers found a way to investigate the problem from another angle. Rather than relying on a single combined measurement, they compared separate polarization maps generated by different groups of detectors.

Recent findings suggest that if cosmic birefringence is real, its effect should appear consistently across all these maps. By comparing the maps with one another, the researchers can effectively eliminate any rotation shared by all of them. What remains reveals differences in the calibration of the individual detector groups, making it possible to identify inconsistencies that might otherwise complicate the search for newly introduced physics.

Sources indicate that "The signal we are looking for is incredibly small, so we have to be certain that we are seeing the universe and not our instrument," said Lonappan. "Our method gives us a complementary way to check that distinction. Before interpreting a tiny rotation as new physics, we want to know that the calibration itself can be trusted.".

Testing the Mystery With Planck Satellite Data.

According to recent reports, to evaluate their technique, the researchers analyzed eight polarization maps produced using Planck observations. They then compared their findings with results from an established approach called the Minami-Komatsu analysis, which is used to distinguish instrumental rotation from possible cosmic birefringence.

Industry observers note that although the two methods rely on different assumptions, they produced consistent results. This agreement provides an vital independent check on how relative detector calibration errors are being assessed.

Recent findings suggest that the new approach also has a deliberate limitation. Because it removes any rotation common to all the maps, it cannot independently measure the overall polarization angle or determine how much the universe itself may have rotated the light. Establishing that absolute rotation still requires an independent reference for calibrating the overall angle.

According to recent reports, to demonstrate how their findings fit with existing measurements, the researchers combined their reconstruction of relative calibration differences with the common calibration value inferred from the established analysis. This produced an estimated cosmic birefringence angle of 0.37 ± 0.12 degrees, matching the Minami-Komatsu result.

Sources indicate that importantly, this agreement does not independently confirm that the ancient light has actually rotated. Instead, it shows that the new method can reproduce results from the existing framework while providing a separate way to examine potential calibration problems.

Searching for Gravitational Waves From the Early Universe.

The technique could also play an important role in another major pursuit in cosmology: the search for gravitational waves generated during the universe's earliest moments.

To understand why, scientists distinguish between two patterns of polarization in the cosmic microwave background, known as E modes and B modes.

Sources indicate that E modes were first detected in 2002. They arise from density variations in the early universe and form symmetric polarization patterns. B modes have a different appearance, featuring patterns that resemble curls or swirls.

Sources indicate that one known source of B modes is gravitational lensing, which occurs when the gravity of matter between Earth and the early universe bends and distorts the path of ancient light. Scientists have already observed B modes created through this process.

However, researchers are also searching for a different kind of B mode that could have been produced by primordial gravitational waves. These ripples in spacetime may have originated during an extremely early period of rapid cosmic expansion, known as inflation. The distinctive B mode signal associated with those primordial gravitational waves has not yet been detected.

Finding it would provide powerful evidence about gravitational waves in the early universe and could offer strong support for particular models of cosmic inflation, potentially transforming scientists' understanding of how the universe began.

Why Extremely Precise Measurements Matter.

Sources indicate that the challenge is that even a slight error in a telescope's polarization calibration can cause some of the much stronger E-mode signal to appear incorrectly as B modes. This contamination could make an instrumental artifact look like an exciting cosmological discovery.

Sources indicate that the UC San Diego method could help prevent such mistakes by identifying differences in polarization angle calibration among detector groups. That makes it a potentially valuable tool for future experiments searching for the extremely faint signatures of primordial gravitational waves.

This kind of independent verification will become increasingly crucial as observatories develop the ability to measure cosmic polarization with greater precision. One example is the Simons Observatory, where Keating serves as principal investigator.

As these instruments become more sensitive, researchers will need equally rigorous methods for confirming that the faint signals they detect are genuine features of the universe rather than imperfections in their equipment.

It has been revealed that "The detection of primordial B modes would transform our understanding of the early universe, so the measurement must survive rigorous calibration checks," noted Keating. "Anto has developed a useful new framework for testing relative polarization-angle calibration. This is ultimately about knowing when we can trust a measurement.".

Beyond the Standard Model: Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

The possibility of cosmic birefringence is particularly fascinating because it could reveal physics that lies beyond the Standard Model.

According to recent reports, although this framework has been remarkably successful at describing fundamental particles and their interactions, it cannot explain everything in the universe. Among its most important unanswered questions are the identity of dark matter and the origin and observed magnitude of dark energy. Together, these mysterious components account for approximately 95% of the universe's total energy density.

According to recent reports, one possible explanation for cosmic birefringence involves a hypothetical field associated with particles resembling axions. Such a field could interact with light and gradually alter its polarization as it crosses the universe. However, these particles have not been confirmed to exist, and they would not necessarily be responsible for dark matter.

Other theoretical explanations connect the possible rotation to fields associated with dark energy, the mysterious phenomenon linked to the accelerating expansion of the universe.

If cosmic birefringence is eventually confirmed, it could provide an entirely upcoming way to investigate these cosmic mysteries and reveal evidence of physical laws beyond those at the moment understood.

For now, the first challenge is ensuring that the subtle signal can be trusted. By giving researchers another way to identify potential measurement errors, the latest technique strengthens the foundation for future discoveries that could reshape our picture of the universe.
